clue.text: Figure one Grand Master must enter with first class marks

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so the one-and-Master letters sit within the figure

blocks.note: a stat is a statistic, a figure
the Roman numeral for one
the standard chess abbreviation
A is a top grade, first class

explanation.surface: A figure skater with a top grade gets a grand master's high marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests a shape or person, but here it is a statistic; first class gives A, as in A1.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are the marks resembling Christ's crucifixion wounds, appearing on a saint's body.

clue.text: Student about to delay getting protection

blocks.note: a tutee is someone taught by a tutor

clue.text: Instinctive to cover fellow’s opening in nearby armed battle

in places the fellow's letter within the nearby word
covering something wraps it, so the instinctive word goes around the rest

blocks.note: a gut reaction is instinctive
nigh is an old word for near
first letter of fellow

explanation.surface: An instinctive urge drives a fellow into a nearby armed battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Two wrappings: the fellow's letter first goes into nearby, then the instinctive word covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunfight is a fight between people shooting guns at each other, an armed exchange.

clue.text: Cautious, having answer misplaced? It’s wrong

blocks.note: being wary is being cautious

explanation.walkthrough: A is the abbreviation for answer; moving it from second place to first turns WARY into AWRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans that go awry turn out badly, so the word means amiss or not as intended.

clue.text: Dreadful article — Times largely diminished

blocks.note: the indefinite article
as in three by four, meaning multiplied
something diminished has been made small

explanation.surface: A newspaper article laments that The Times has shrunk badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign BY. SMALL loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means extremely bad or appalling, as in an abysmal performance.

clue.text: Looked to consume whisky and brandy, finally out of touch with reality

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word before it
consuming something takes it inside, so the looked word swallows the drinks

blocks.note: to stare is to look fixedly
rye is a kind of whisky
last letter of brandy

explanation.surface: A drinker downed whisky and brandy and ended up detached from reality.
explanation.walkthrough: Rye is a North American whisky distilled mainly from rye grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being starry-eyed means being naively idealistic or dreamy, not seeing things as they truly are.

clue.text: Get hold of drink, say, in Canadian city

a nip is a small drink of spirits
e.g. means for example, as does say

explanation.definitionFit: Winnipeg is the capital of the province of Manitoba in central Canada.

clue.text: Workers in carbon and iron and different elements

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Carbon and iron are chemical elements, and the clue lists metalworkers handling them.
explanation.walkthrough: Steel is an alloy of iron with a little carbon, so the definition describes the material by its recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Steelmen are steelworkers, people employed making steel, which is iron alloyed with carbon.

clue.text: In flight, bat is not a plant-fancier

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A flying bat is said not to be a plant lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In flight' suits the bat in the surface, but it signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanist studies plants scientifically, so fancying plants is a playful way to describe the profession.

clue.text: Sea dweller not entirely near a bit of sun

explanation.definitionFit: The Sorbonne is the famous historic university in Paris, an academic institution.

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Astute, flushing it out

blocks.note: taken as written

M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.walkthrough: 'Going to' means the M is placed after SPA. A maiden in cricket is an over in which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is junk email sent in bulk, so it is a mass of unsolicited messages.

clue.text: Medical man’s impression about twisted pose

to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist is a practitioner of dental medicine, a health professional who treats teeth.

clue.text: Small party walked up for crustaceans

blocks.note: standard abbreviation

to pace is to walk steadily

explanation.definitionFit: Decapods are ten-legged crustaceans, the order containing crabs, lobsters and shrimps.

clue.text: Lack of difficulties about French at a basic level

blocks.note: no ills means no troubles
standard abbreviation

standard abbreviation

clue.text: Last of huntsmen considering ignoring first sound of horses

weighing something up is considering it

clue.text: Small quantity of grasses, mostly rudimentary

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grasses' looks like plants, but it is the verb for informing; to grass is British slang for to inform on someone, and Oates is history's famous informer.

clue.text: Fairly big Scottish town containing one hospital

the Roman numeral for one
